 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - The National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) has issued Circular Letter (SE) Number 4 of 2026 regarding Preparedness Measures for the Upcoming Rainy Season 2026/2027 on October 30, 2026.
 BNPB Chief Lieutenant General Kristomei Sianturi stated that the SE is distributed to governors, mayors, and regents across Indonesia to anticipate potential flooding during the rainy season.
 "I also urge all governors, regents, and local leaders to be vigilant regarding the flood risks in their respective areas," Kristomei remarked while leading a Review Meeting on Weather Modification Operations (OMC) in handling forest and land fires at the Integrated Post, Base Ops Halim Perdanakusuma, Jakarta, on Monday (2/11/2026), as quoted in his statement.
 This SE was issued to anticipate potential risks of hydrometeorological disasters expected during the rainy season, predicted to begin at the end of 2026.
 It is hoped that local governments can enhance their vigilance and readiness of personnel, equipment, and community capacity in their respective areas.
 He emphasized that some regions have already experienced flooding. Therefore, he requested all parties to be alert for the transition from the dry season to the rainy season.
 "The challenges seem to be shifting; after forest and land fires, we now have flooding. Let's prepare together," Kristomei stated.
 KOMPAS.com/EKO AGUS HERIANTO Illustration of flooding in Medan City due to rising river levels. 
 Rainy Season Forecast
 Previously, the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency ( BMKG ) estimated that the rainy season in Indonesia will gradually begin in November 2026.
 The regions expected to experience the rainy season from November include parts of Sumatra, parts of Java, parts of Kalimantan, parts of Bali, parts of West Nusa Tenggara (NTB), a small part of East Nusa Tenggara (NTT), parts of Sulawesi, parts of North Maluku, parts of Maluku, northern West Papua, and parts of southern Papua.
 "Most of Indonesia is predicted to enter the rainy season in November 2026, covering 185 seasonal zones or 24.66 percent of Indonesia's land area," said BMKG Chairman Teuku Faisal Fathani at a press conference, as reported from the BMKG YouTube broadcast on Tuesday (22/9/2026).
 Furthermore, during December 2026, the rainy season is expected to occur in 266 seasonal zones or 17.31 percent of Indonesia's land area.
 In December, parts of Lampung, most of Java, parts of South Kalimantan, most of Bali, most of NTB, most of NTT, most of Sulawesi, parts of North Maluku, parts of Maluku, and southern Papua are predicted to experience the rainy season.
 "The onset of the rainy season in some regions in Indonesia is predicted to arrive later than expected, specifically in 529 zones or 61.08 percent of Indonesia's land area," Faisal noted.
 BMKG predicts that the majority of Indonesia will reach the peak of the rainy season in December 2026.
 This peak in December 2026 is expected to affect 155 zones or 36.94 percent of Indonesia's land area.
 Subsequently, in January 2027, the peak of the rainy season is anticipated to occur in 162 seasonal zones or 25.68 percent of Indonesia's land area.
